messages:
devon: Hey — running the Node quickstart on a Windows dev box (PowerShell) behind corp proxy, using a service-account key we got from infra. First call returns a 402 JSON error: {"error":"payment_required", "message":"workspace billing not configured"}. Anyone seen this with service accounts?

maya: Hm, 402 usually means the workspace that the key is scoped to has no billing profile. Can you paste the curl/CLI command you used (no secrets)? Also which token type is it (service account vs personal API key)?

devon: Using the quickstart curl from docs: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/completions \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer svc_XXXX" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-base","prompt":"hello"}'
```
Response: 402, body: `{"error":"payment_required","detail":"workspace 01G... has no billing profile"}`

sam: Two quick checks: 1) is the svc token scoped to a workspace/org that actually has billing set up? 2) are you accidentally sending the token for another org (happens with local env vars). On Windows sometimes folks set REDWOOD_API_KEY in system env vs user env and process picks a different one.

devon: Token came from infra team service account for project "infra-sandbox". I assumed infra had billing. How can I verify which workspace this token maps to?

maya: You can hit the /v1/whoami endpoint (non-destructive) to see identity and workspace: 
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer svc_XXXX" https://api.redwood.example/v1/whoami
```
That will show workspace id and role — if billing missing, you’ll see the workspace id in the 402 detail too.

devon: Ran whoami and it shows workspace 01G123 (infra-sandbox). infra-sandbox is indeed missing a billing profile. Oops.

sam: OK two options: A) attach billing to infra-sandbox workspace (infra/fin team action) or B) for local dev, use your personal dev token attached to a workspace with billing or free credits. Also for immediate workaround you can run the quickstart against the demo workspace if allowed.

devon: I didn’t want to escalate to finance right now. I tried switching to my personal key and the same curl now returns 200 and body with choices. First successful call! :tada:

maya: Nice. We should add a short note in the quickstart about service accounts requiring a billing-enabled workspace — a lot of new devs hit this. Can you open a tiny DX PR to the docs?

devon: Yup will do. Also adding note for Windows developers: set env with `setx REDWOOD_API_KEY "..."` and then open a new shell — otherwise processes might pick an older value.

devex-bot: New docs PR opened by devon: #432 - "quickstart: service-account billing note"

sam: Thanks — marking this thread as resolved. If infra wants us to validate their service accounts we can run a quick script that checks whoami and billing state to catch these before hand.

devon: Good idea. I'll follow up with infra and open a small check script in the infra repo.
